title: TIL, Veo 3 Can Animate Sprites
author: Mean_Establishment31
selftext:
Just add the reference pixel image using Frames in the Google Flow view and tell it how you want it to animate:

https://preview.redd.it/apcjih49b65f1.png?width=1201&format=png&auto=webp&s=5d043d1573238a8ae7644efe02ed429ecc466b0d

https://i.redd.it/7w4fgf3bb65f1.gif

comments.author: DefenderNeverender
comments.body: This would be an absolute game changer for me, who can make pixel art but animate like I have banana hands.

replies.author: Alone-Amphibian2434
replies.body: bad animation is going to be an asset in the future, will be the only way we know some art is bespoke

comments.author: Baphaddon
comments.body: This is arguably worth the $250 price point. Is it still costing that much?

replies.author: Mean_Establishment31
replies.body: It’s $150 or so for the first 3 months atm

replies.author: Quind1
replies.body: I tried animating stills of 3D models I created (non-AI) that I've been struggling to rig, and this created a pretty decent walk cycle. I set the modeling software to use a chroma key, which possibly helped, but my first generation looked pretty good. I have to say, this probably is worth the money as it's a huge time saver.

replies.author: pickedyouflowers
replies.body: not. i tried for 2 yrs to get this, SD will NOT be able to get this. Diffusion is random by it's nature thus you will have inconsistencies between frames, theres no way around it. Maybe FLUX but not xl/1.5

comments.author: Optimal-Fix1216
comments.body: I don't think veo 3 takes references yet. You sure that isn't veo 2?

replies.author: Mean_Establishment31
replies.body: I’m just using frames in the flow UI and selecting highest quality (V3). I can tell it is v3 also because there are sound effects :)

comments.author: -RoopeSeta-
comments.body: Is there anything close to Veo 3 in eu?

comments.author: Itchy_Mycologist_513
comments.body: How would you get rid of the white background?

replies.author: Mean_Establishment31
replies.body: Texture Packer or Photoshop. I believe Flux Konyext can also do it.

comments.author: Itchy_Mycologist_513
comments.body: How would you get rid of the white background?

replies.author: Mean_Establishment31
replies.body: To clarify, Veo3 can export the animation as a gif

replies.author: TzarineJador
replies.body: Can it do a transparent gif?

replies.author: Mean_Establishment31
replies.body: Not to my knowledge, but there are plenty of programs that allow you to break out the frames of a gif and make it transparent. Photoshop / Texture Packer being some of them.

replies.author: TzarineJador
replies.body: Okay yea cool! I use Photoshop now so easy enough. Was curious about what's out of the box.

comments.author: LionaltheGreat
comments.body:
I am a gamedev novice but have been experimenting with the same thing, since I’m not an animator!

How could I take the exported gif or mp4 from geo and turn it into an animation that can play in my game? Do I need to extract all the frames of something??

replies.author: Mean_Establishment31
replies.body: Texture Packer is great for this. There is an option to split / slice frames or something like that, which automates the process. Just ask GPT for the details

comments.body: can it do like regular 2d animation, not pixel art?
